questions.stem: A motor vehicle battery is best described as a
options: primary cell battery that is thrown away when flat
device that generates electricity from engine rotation
capacitor that stores charge on two metal plates
secondary cell battery that stores energy chemically and can be recharged
questions.explanation: A lead-acid vehicle battery is made of secondary (rechargeable) cells; the alternator, not the battery, generates electricity from engine rotation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MAIN use of the battery in a petrol car?
options: Supplying current to the starter motor to crank the engine
questions.explanation: The battery's main job is to supply the large cranking current; once the engine runs the alternator supplies the load and charges the battery.

questions.topic: Types, constructional details and ratings of battery
questions.stem: In a fully charged lead-acid cell, the positive plate is made of
questions.explanation: The positive plate is chocolate-brown lead peroxide (PbO2) and the negative plate is grey spongy lead; nickel and cadmium are used in alkaline cells.

questions.topic: Types, constructional details and ratings of battery
questions.stem: The electrolyte used in a nickel-cadmium (nickel-alkaline) cell is
questions.explanation: Nickel-alkaline cells use potassium hydroxide; dilute sulphuric acid is the lead-acid electrolyte.

questions.topic: Types, constructional details and ratings of battery
questions.stem: A fully charged 12-volt lead-acid battery has six cells connected in series, each giving about 2.1 V on open circuit. The open-circuit voltage of the battery is about
questions.explanation: Cells in series add their voltages: 6 x 2.1 V = 12.6 V.

questions.topic: Types, constructional details and ratings of battery
questions.stem: A battery is rated at 72 Ah at the 20-hour rate. What steady current can it supply for 20 hours?
questions.explanation: Current = capacity / time = 72 Ah / 20 h = 3.6 A.

questions.stem: When preparing electrolyte for a lead-acid battery, the technician must always
options: pour the distilled water quickly into the concentrated acid
pour the concentrated acid slowly into the distilled water
mix the acid with tap water in a metal bucket
heat the acid before adding water
questions.explanation: Adding acid to water slowly lets the heat disperse; adding water to acid can boil violently and spatter acid.

questions.stem: Batteries on charge must be kept away from naked flames and sparks because charging gives off
questions.explanation: Charging electrolyses water in the electrolyte into hydrogen and oxygen, an explosive mixture.

questions.stem: A hydrometer reading of about 1.270 in every cell of a lead-acid battery shows that the battery is
questions.explanation: Relative density of about 1.26 to 1.28 indicates full charge; about 1.10 to 1.12 indicates a flat cell.

questions.stem: One cell of a battery gives a hydrometer reading of 1.150 while the other five read 1.270 after a full charge. The most likely conclusion is that
options: the battery is fully charged and serviceable
the low cell is faulty (e.g. shorted plates) and the battery should be replaced
all cells need topping up with acid
the charging rate was too low for all cells
questions.explanation: A cell that stays low after charging while others are full indicates an internal fault such as a short or sulphated plates.

questions.topic: Purpose and components of starting system
questions.stem: The purpose of the starting system is to
options: crank the engine fast enough for it to start running on its own
questions.explanation: The starter turns the flywheel until combustion takes over; charging and sparks are other systems.

questions.topic: Purpose and components of starting system
questions.stem: The starter solenoid is used mainly to
options: close the heavy-current contacts to the starter motor using a small switch current
reduce the voltage supplied to the starter
store charge for the next start
questions.explanation: The ignition switch carries only a small current to the solenoid, whose plunger closes the heavy contacts that carry hundreds of amperes.

questions.stem: A starter motor takes 1.8 kW from a 12 V battery. The current in the main starter cable is
questions.explanation: I = P / V = 1800 W / 12 V = 150 A, which is why starter cables are very thick and short.

questions.stem: In the starting circuit, the thick main cable runs from the battery positive terminal to the
questions.explanation: Heavy current goes battery to solenoid to motor; only a light cable runs from the ignition switch to the solenoid.

questions.stem: In an inertia (Bendix) type starter drive, the pinion moves into mesh with the flywheel ring gear because
options: a solenoid lever pushes it before the motor turns
the whole armature slides along its axis
a spring holds it permanently in mesh
the pinion lags behind the spinning shaft and is screwed along a helix
questions.explanation: When the motor spins suddenly the pinion's inertia makes it run along the helical sleeve into mesh; lever engagement is the pre-engaged type and sliding armature is the axial type.

questions.stem: The roller (overrunning) clutch in a pre-engaged starter motor
options: prevents the engine from driving the armature at excessive speed after the engine starts
reduces the current drawn by the solenoid
holds the pinion out of mesh during cranking
questions.explanation: Once the engine fires the ring gear tries to drive the pinion very fast; the overrunning clutch freewheels so the armature is not over-speeded.

questions.stem: The commutator of a starter motor armature that is slightly burnt and grooved should be
options: skimmed in a lathe and cleaned with fine glass paper
filed with a coarse bastard file
questions.explanation: Light skimming restores a true surface; coarse files damage it and varnish would insulate the brushes from the segments.

questions.topic: Purpose and components of ignition system
questions.stem: In a contact-breaker ignition system, the component that distributes high-tension current to each sparking plug in turn is the
questions.explanation: The rotor arm turns inside the cap and passes the HT pulse to each plug lead in firing order.

questions.topic: Purpose and components of ignition system
questions.stem: The capacitor (condenser) connected across the contact-breaker points
options: raises the battery voltage to 12 V
reduces arcing at the points and speeds up the collapse of the magnetic field
questions.explanation: Absorbing the self-induced current reduces point burning and gives a faster field collapse, so a higher secondary voltage.

questions.stem: In the ignition circuit diagram, the low-tension (primary) circuit consists of the battery, ignition switch, coil primary winding and
questions.explanation: The primary circuit is the low-voltage path switched by the points; HT leads, cap, rotor and plugs are on the secondary side.

questions.topic: Construction and operation of ignition coil
questions.stem: An ignition coil has 250 primary turns and 20000 secondary turns. If 300 V is induced in the primary when the points open, the ideal secondary voltage is

questions.topic: Construction and operation of ignition coil
questions.stem: Compared with the primary winding, the secondary winding of an ignition coil has
options: no turns, only an iron core
many more turns of much thinner wire
questions.explanation: The step-up action needs many thousands of fine turns on the secondary; the primary has a few hundred turns of thicker wire.

questions.stem: One advantage of electronic ignition over the contact-breaker type is that
options: there are no points to wear, so the timing stays accurate longer
it does not need sparking plugs
it works without an ignition coil
questions.explanation: A magnetic or Hall-effect trigger replaces the points, removing wear and burning; plugs and coil are still needed.

questions.stem: A four-cylinder four-stroke engine runs at 3000 rev/min. How many sparks per second must the ignition system produce?
questions.explanation: Each cylinder fires once every two revolutions: 3000 x 4 / 2 = 6000 sparks per minute = 100 per second.

questions.stem: Pinking (knocking) when the engine is accelerated under load is a typical sign that the ignition timing is
questions.explanation: Over-advanced timing makes peak pressure occur too early and causes detonation; retarded timing mainly gives sluggish performance and poor economy.

questions.stem: A good spark is obtained at the end of the coil HT lead but not at any plug lead. The fault is most likely in the
questions.explanation: Since HT reaches the coil lead, the primary side works; the break must lie between the coil lead and plug leads, i.e. rotor or cap.

questions.topic: Purpose and components of charging system
questions.stem: Which component in the charging system limits the alternator output voltage to about 14 V?
questions.explanation: The regulator controls field current to hold output at about 14 V; diodes only rectify.

questions.stem: In a vehicle alternator, the magnetic field is produced by the
options: stator winding, fed through a commutator
rotor winding, fed through brushes and slip rings
questions.explanation: The rotating field winding receives current through brushes and slip rings; the three-phase output is generated in the stationary stator.

questions.stem: A three-phase vehicle alternator uses six main diodes in its rectifier in order to
options: give full-wave rectification of all three phases
give half-wave rectification of one phase
raise the output voltage to 24 V
supply alternating current to the battery
questions.explanation: Two diodes per phase (positive and negative) give full-wave three-phase rectification; batteries need direct current.

questions.stem: A circuit diagram of the charging system is useful to the technician because it
options: shows the exact colour of the car
shows how components are connected so faults can be traced systematically
replaces the need for a multimeter
gives the price of each component
questions.explanation: Diagrams show the connection paths and terminals, allowing logical fault tracing.

questions.stem: The ignition (charge) warning lamp stays on while the engine runs at speed. A likely cause is
options: a slipping or broken alternator drive belt
questions.explanation: If the belt slips the alternator does not produce output, so the warning lamp stays lit.

questions.topic: Purpose and classification of lighting in a motor vehicle
questions.stem: Which of the following is a NON-obligatory light on a motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: Fog and spot lamps are optional extras; tail, stop and number-plate lamps are required by law.

questions.stem: A halogen headlamp bulb can run its filament hotter than an ordinary bulb because the halogen gas
options: reduces the voltage across the filament
returns evaporated tungsten to the filament
questions.explanation: The halogen cycle redeposits evaporated tungsten onto the filament, so it can run hotter and brighter without blackening the glass.

questions.stem: Two 55 W, 12 V headlamp bulbs are switched on together. The total current drawn is about
questions.explanation: I = total power / voltage = 110 W / 12 V = 9.2 A; this guides fuse and cable selection.

questions.stem: In a vehicle lighting circuit, the side lamps, tail lamps and number-plate lamps are connected in
options: series, so that they share the voltage
parallel, so that one bulb failing does not put out the others
parallel with the starter motor only
questions.explanation: Vehicle lamps are in parallel so each gets full battery voltage and works independently.

questions.topic: Maintenance and repairs of lighting system
questions.stem: Both headlamps work on main beam but neither works on dipped beam. The most probable fault is
options: a faulty dip switch or its dipped-beam supply wire
two blown fuses for the side lamps
questions.explanation: A fault common to both dipped filaments points to the shared dip switch or feed, since two filaments rarely fail together.

questions.topic: Concept and components of auxiliary system
questions.stem: Which of these is part of the auxiliary system of a motor vehicle?
questions.explanation: Auxiliary units are additional electrical devices such as wipers, horn, gauges and washers.

questions.topic: Constructional details and operation of auxiliary system components
questions.stem: The water temperature sender unit commonly contains a thermistor whose resistance
options: increases as the coolant temperature rises
decreases as the coolant temperature rises
questions.explanation: An NTC thermistor passes more current to the gauge as temperature rises, so the needle moves towards hot.

questions.topic: Constructional details and operation of auxiliary system components
questions.stem: A horn relay is fitted in the horn circuit so that
options: the horn sounds louder by raising voltage
the horn push carries only a small current while the relay contacts carry the heavy horn current
the horn works without a battery
the horn sounds only at night
questions.explanation: The relay protects the horn button and allows short heavy-gauge feed wiring to the horn.

questions.topic: Maintenance and repairs of auxiliary components
questions.stem: The oil pressure warning lamp stays on with the engine running, but a mechanical gauge fitted temporarily shows normal pressure. The fault is most likely
options: a faulty oil pressure switch or an earth fault in its wire
questions.explanation: Since actual pressure is normal, the warning circuit is at fault: the switch is stuck closed or its wire is shorted to earth.

questions.topic: Types, constructional details and ratings of battery
questions.stem:
(a) Describe the construction of a 12 V lead-acid battery, naming five main parts. [7 marks]
(b) Explain what is meant by the ampere-hour rating of a battery. [3 marks]
(c) A 60 Ah battery supplies a constant load of 4 A. Calculate how long it will last, assuming the full rated capacity is available. [3 marks]
(d) State two differences between a lead-acid cell and a nickel-alkaline cell. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Six cells in series in a moulded container, connected by inter-cell connectors to two terminal posts
5 marks: (a) Any five parts, 1 mark each: container/case; positive plates (lead peroxide); negative plates (spongy lead); separators; electrolyte (dilute sulphuric acid); cell connectors; terminal posts; vent plugs; lid
3 marks: (b) The quantity of electricity the battery can deliver: steady current multiplied by the hours it can be sustained (usually at the 20-hour rate) before the cell voltage falls to about 1.75 V
3 marks: (c) t = Ah / I = 60 / 4 (2) = 15 hours (1)
2 marks: (d) Any two, 1 mark each: electrolyte sulphuric acid vs potassium hydroxide; cell voltage about 2 V vs 1.2 V; lead plates vs nickel/cadmium plates; alkaline cell is lighter in duty, longer life and tolerates overcharge
questions.explanation: Six 2 V cells in series in a case with lead peroxide positive plates, spongy lead negative plates, separators and dilute sulphuric acid, joined by connectors to terminals, with vent plugs. Ah rating = current x hours deliverable. 60 Ah / 4 A = 15 h. Lead-acid uses H2SO4 and gives 2 V per cell; nickel-alkaline uses KOH and gives 1.2 V per cell.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe how a hydrometer is used to test the state of charge of a battery. [6 marks]
(b) State three symptoms of an over-charged battery. [3 marks]
(c) State four precautions for the safe keeping of an idle battery. [4 marks]
(d) Why is distilled water, not tap water, used for topping up? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a) Remove vent plug (1); squeeze bulb and insert nozzle in electrolyte (1); release bulb to draw electrolyte until float rises freely (1); read float at eye level at the liquid surface (1); compare: about 1.27 full, about 1.20 half, about 1.12 flat (1); return electrolyte to the same cell and repeat for every cell (1)
3 marks: (b) Any three, 1 mark each: excessive gassing/bubbling; rapid loss of water from electrolyte; battery case hot; buckled plates/shedding of paste; corroded terminals
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: keep fully charged and recharge periodically; store in a cool dry place; keep top clean and dry; disconnect leads; keep electrolyte level above plates; store upright off a damp floor
2 marks: (d) Tap water contains dissolved minerals/impurities which contaminate the electrolyte and cause self-discharge and plate damage
questions.explanation: Draw electrolyte into the hydrometer until the float is free, read at eye level, compare with 1.27 (full) to 1.12 (flat), return the sample and test each cell. Over-charging: heavy gassing, water loss, heat, buckled plates. Idle battery: keep charged, cool, clean, disconnected, level correct. Distilled water avoids impurities that cause self-discharge.

questions.stem:
(a) State the purpose of the starting system and list four of its components. [5 marks]
(b) Describe the operation of a pre-engaged starter motor from the moment the ignition key is turned to "start". [6 marks]
(c) State four faults that may prevent a starter motor from cranking the engine. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) To rotate (crank) the engine until it can run on its own
4 marks: (a) Any four, 1 mark each: battery; ignition/starter switch; solenoid; starter motor; flywheel ring gear; heavy cables/earth strap
6 marks: (b) Key energises solenoid pull-in and hold-in windings (1); plunger moves and the engagement lever pushes pinion into mesh with ring gear (1); at end of travel plunger closes main contacts (1); heavy current flows to motor, which cranks the engine (1); when engine fires, roller clutch overruns to protect armature (1); key released, solenoid de-energises and spring withdraws pinion and opens contacts (1)
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: flat battery; loose/corroded terminals or earth strap; faulty solenoid; worn brushes; burnt commutator/open armature; faulty ignition switch; seized engine/jammed pinion
questions.explanation: The starting system cranks the engine; components are battery, switch, solenoid, starter motor, ring gear and cables. Turning the key energises the solenoid, which pushes the pinion into mesh and then closes the main contacts; the motor cranks; the overrunning clutch protects the armature; release returns the pinion. Faults: flat battery, bad connections, faulty solenoid, worn brushes, burnt commutator, faulty switch.

questions.topic: Construction and operation of ignition coil
questions.stem:
(a) With the aid of a labelled description, explain the construction of an ignition coil. [5 marks]
(b) Explain how a high voltage is produced when the contact-breaker points open. [5 marks]
(c) Distinguish between retarded and over-advanced ignition timing, giving one effect of each. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
5 marks: (a) Laminated soft iron core (1); secondary winding of many thousands of turns of fine enamelled wire wound next to the core (1); primary winding of a few hundred turns of thicker wire over it (1); windings in an oil- or resin-filled insulated case (1); terminals: two LT terminals and one HT centre tower (1)
5 marks: (b) With points closed, current flows in primary and builds a magnetic field in the core (1); points open and primary current stops suddenly (1); field collapses rapidly, helped by the capacitor (1); the changing flux cuts the many secondary turns and induces a very high voltage by mutual induction (1); high voltage passes via rotor and cap to the plug and jumps the gap as a spark (1)
2 marks: (c) Retarded: spark occurs too late in the compression stroke; effect - loss of power, overheating, poor fuel economy (any one)
3 marks: (c) Over-advanced: spark occurs too early before TDC (1); effects - pinking/knocking, overheating, possible piston damage, kick-back when starting (any one) (1); correct timing gives maximum pressure just after TDC (1)
questions.explanation: The coil has a laminated iron core with a fine secondary winding of many thousands of turns and a thicker primary of a few hundred turns, sealed in an insulated case. Primary current builds a field; when the points open the field collapses quickly (helped by the capacitor) and induces a very high secondary voltage that fires the plug. Retarded timing fires too late (power loss, overheating); over-advanced fires too early (knocking, piston damage).

questions.stem:
(a) List five main parts of an alternator and state the function of each. [10 marks]
(b) Explain why the output of an alternator must be rectified before it is supplied to the battery. [2 marks]
(c) State three faults in the charging system and one remedy for each. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: (a) Any five, 2 marks each: rotor/field winding - produces rotating magnetic field; stator - three-phase windings in which a.c. is induced; slip rings and brushes - carry field current to rotor; rectifier (diode pack) - converts a.c. to d.c.; voltage regulator - keeps output at about 14 V; fan - cools alternator; pulley - driven by engine belt; bearings - support rotor; drive-end and slip-ring-end brackets - house the parts
2 marks: (b) The alternator produces alternating current, but a battery can only be charged by direct current and vehicle electronics need d.c.
3 marks: (c) Any three, 1 mark each (fault with remedy): slipping belt - adjust/replace belt; worn brushes - replace brushes; open/shorted diode - replace rectifier; seized bearing - replace bearing; faulty regulator - replace regulator; loose connections - clean and tighten
questions.explanation: Rotor (field), stator (output windings), slip rings and brushes (field feed), rectifier (a.c. to d.c.), regulator (limits voltage), fan, pulley and bearings. Rectification is needed because a battery charges only on d.c. Faults: slipping belt, worn brushes, failed diodes, seized bearings, faulty regulator, each repaired by adjustment or replacement.

questions.topic: Constructional details and operation of auxiliary system components
questions.stem:
(a) Define the auxiliary system of a motor vehicle and list four auxiliary units. [5 marks]
(b) Describe the operation of a fuel gauge that uses a float-operated variable resistor (sender) in the tank. [6 marks]
(c) The horn of a car fails to sound. State four checks a technician should make. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) The group of additional electrical devices that provide information, comfort, convenience and safety apart from the starting, ignition, charging and lighting systems
4 marks: (a) Any four, 1 mark each: horn; wipers; screen washer; fuel gauge; temperature gauge; oil pressure gauge/lamp; direction indicators; door switch/courtesy light; heater blower
6 marks: (b) Float rests on fuel surface and moves with the level (1); float arm moves a wiper over a variable resistor (1); resistance changes with fuel level (1); sender is in series with the gauge on the dashboard, fed through the ignition switch (1); current through the gauge changes with resistance (1); gauge pointer deflects to show full or empty (1)
4 marks: (c) Any four, 1 mark each: check the fuse; check the horn relay; check horn push/earth contact; test for voltage at horn terminals with a test lamp/multimeter; check horn earth; check/adjust horn or replace if faulty
questions.explanation: Auxiliary system: extra devices such as horn, wipers, washer, gauges, indicators. Fuel gauge: float moves a wiper on a resistor in the tank; the changing resistance changes current through the gauge, moving its pointer. Horn failure: check fuse, relay, horn push and earth, voltage at horn, then the horn itself.
